question: What is the primary purpose of a community diagnosis?

options.A: To evaluate the health status and needs of a defined population
options.B: To audit the financial records of a primary health care clinic
options.C: To assign medical doctors to specific local government areas
options.D: To treat individual chronic diseases in a hospital setting

explanation: A community diagnosis looks broadly at an entire group to identify overall health status, risk factors, and health needs. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why is a community diagnosis compared to an individual physical assessment?

options.A: Both require invasive laboratory testing before any action can be taken
options.B: Both are performed only when a patient is admitted to an intensive care unit
options.C: Both gather baseline data to guide targeted interventions and care planning
options.D: Both focus exclusively on genetic predispositions and family history

explanation: Just as an individual assessment informs a patient's nursing care plan, a community assessment guides public health interventions. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of community entry during a health assessment?

options.A: Collecting blood samples from every household in the community
options.B: Immediately administering medications to treat prevalent infectious diseases
options.C: Constructing permanent primary health care clinics in the local area
options.D: Building trust and securing cooperation from local leaders and residents

explanation: Community entry focuses on establishing rapport and gaining the acceptance of local gatekeepers before gathering data. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why is recruiting local data collectors vital during the preparatory phase?

options.A: They have the legal authority to enforce mandatory health quarantine
options.B: They provide all the financial funding required for the project
options.C: They possess advanced degrees in epidemiological data management
options.D: They understand the local language, customs, and cultural nuances

explanation: Local collectors bridge communication gaps and reduce suspicion, ensuring more accurate and respectful data gathering. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which data collection method involves a structured door-to-door questionnaire?
explanation: Household surveys use standardized questionnaires administered across residences to gather broad quantitative demographic and health data. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h3)

question: A nurse wants to understand why mothers in a rural village reject routine immunization despite available vaccines. Which method is most appropriate?
explanation: Qualitative methods like focus groups allow community members to openly discuss cultural beliefs, fears, and attitudes shaping health behaviors. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h3)

question: What is the very first step in conducting a community diagnosis?

options.A: Purchasing medical equipment for a health clinic
options.B: Writing the final evaluation report for the ministry
options.C: Analyzing statistical data using computer software
options.D: Defining the community boundaries and target population

explanation: Before collecting data, the scope of the assessment must be set by clearly defining the target population and geographical limits. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why is the validation step included near the end of a community diagnosis?

options.A: To confirm findings with community members and ensure data accuracy
options.B: To calculate the total financial cost of the intervention phase
options.C: To distribute free prescription drugs to participating households
options.D: To legally enforce mandatory health policies across the region

explanation: Validation sessions involve sharing draft results with local leaders to correct misinterpretations and secure community buy-in. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h4)

question: What does data analysis in a community diagnosis primarily involve?

options.A: Conducting door-to-door interviews with local market traders
options.B: Calculating frequencies, rates, and ratios to identify health patterns
options.C: Administering therapeutic treatments to individual hospital patients
options.D: Drafting legal documents for the local government council

explanation: Data analysis compiles raw numbers into statistical metrics that highlight disease distribution and health trends. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h5)

question: How do environmental sanitation deficits become evident during data analysis?

options.A: By interviewing hospital doctors about their personal salary structures
options.B: By counting the number of registered vehicles in the community
options.C: By correlating high rates of waterborne illness with poor access to clean water
options.D: By measuring the average height of school-aged children

explanation: Analyzing multiple variables together reveals underlying environmental causes contributing to specific disease burdens. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h5)

question: Which criterion is generally used to prioritize health problems in a community?

options.A: Availability of international air travel to the region
options.B: Political party affiliation of the local council chairman
options.C: Personal preference of the lead public health nurse
options.D: Magnitude and severity of the health condition

explanation: Prioritization relies on objective criteria like how many people are affected (magnitude) and how severely their health is impacted. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h6)

question: Why is feasibility an important consideration when ranking community health needs?

options.A: It ensures that problems can realistically be addressed with available resources
options.B: It guarantees that every single disease in the community will be eradicated
options.C: It eliminates the need for community participation in health programs
options.D: It prevents the government from spending money on public infrastructure

explanation: Feasibility assesses whether interventions are practical given local financial, material, and human constraints. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h6)

question: What core component must every community action plan include?

options.A: Specific objectives, timelines, and assigned responsibilities
options.B: International funding grants from foreign health organizations
options.C: Guaranteed lifetime employment contracts for all healthcare staff
options.D: Comprehensive architectural blueprints for large hospitals

explanation: An action plan details what will be done, who will do it, when it will happen, and what resources are needed. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h7)

question: Why is top-down imposition of health interventions discouraged during action planning?

options.A: It requires too many medical doctors to work in rural health posts
options.B: It prevents nurses from conducting private clinical consultations
options.C: It often leads to low community acceptance and poor program sustainability
options.D: It violates international maritime trade and health regulations

explanation: Programs designed without local input frequently fail because they do not align with community values or daily realities. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h7)

question: What is the primary difference between monitoring and evaluation?

options.A: Monitoring focuses on finances, while evaluation focuses on buildings
options.B: Monitoring is done only by doctors, while evaluation is done by patients
options.C: Monitoring requires laboratory testing, while evaluation uses surveys
options.D: Monitoring tracks ongoing activities, while evaluation assesses final outcomes

explanation: Monitoring occurs during the project to ensure tasks are on track, whereas evaluation measures the overall success and impact after completion. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h8)

question: Why is post-intervention evaluation compared against baseline community diagnosis data?

options.A: To measure what changes and improvements occurred as a result of the program
options.B: To prove that no diseases existed in the community prior to the project
options.C: To justify closing down the local primary health care clinic
options.D: To determine which health workers deserve a salary bonus

explanation: Baseline data provides a starting point against which post-intervention indicators are compared to determine real health impact. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h8)
